subject: Post-demo: model slate & cost/latency/quality rationale for Chalice
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: James Liao <james@chalice.ai>, Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@chalice.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model slate & cost/latency/quality rationale for Chalice

Hi James / Anna —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful to see Chalice's 1) low-latency inference requirement for live chat and 2) strict throughput burst profile during peak concurrent sessions. Based on our run bench and the prompt examples you shared, I put together a pragmatic candidate slate that balances your latency SLO (<=200ms median per-token in production), token cost target, and tolerance for occasional quality regressions during canary rollouts. Attaching the short prompt pack and bench PDF for reference.

Recommended shortlist (ordered by operational fit):
- rw-infer-mistral-7b-fp16 (baseline) — Best cost/latency for 95% of conversational path; strong instruction-following on our prompt set.
- rw-infer-gptj-13b-8bit (quality-first) — ~2–3x higher cost but materially better on long-context coherence for your summarization route. Good candidate for higher-value calls or A/B.
- rw-infer-llama2-70b-quant (fallback for quality-sensitive requests) — higher latency/cost; keep behind routing rule for requests flagged as high-criticality.

Bench highlights (see attached PDF):
- Mistral-7b-fp16: median per-token latency 45ms @ 50 concurrent streams (p50), cost estimate ~$120 / 1M tokens.
- GPTJ-13b-8bit: median per-token latency 110ms @ 25 concurrent; cost estimate ~$340 / 1M tokens.
- Llama2-70b-quant: median per-token latency 320ms @ 10 concurrent; cost estimate ~$980 / 1M tokens.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary + Regression Guardrails: start with Mistral-7b on 100% of low-value traffic, run GPTJ-13b on 10% canary traffic for quality validation using the regression prompt set (attached). If mean QA score delta < 0.06 after 48h, expand GPTJ traffic to 30% for higher-conversion routes.
- Routing policy: route by route-type (chat_short vs. summarize_long) and by customer-tier (free vs. premium) to control unit economics.
- Caching & Prefix KV: enable prefix caching for system prompts & static instructions — should cut token spend by ~12–18% for your steady-state.
- Quantization path: test 4-bit quant for GPTJ candidate in a staging run to see if latency improvement justifies minor quality loss on longer threads.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Sync to lock the two pilot routes (chat_short, summarize_long) and sample sizes.
2) We’ll spin a 2-week eval cluster with telemetry + regression tests (Redwood provides the draft test harness).
3) Procurement: I'll loop in our sales ops for a 3-month pilot pricing sheet once you confirm the routes.

Attachments: chalice_prompt_set_v1.csv; bench_results_chalice_20280601.pdf; recommended_engines_cost_model.xlsx

Thanks — happy to talk through the tradeoffs live. Are you available Mon 6/4 10–11am PT for a short alignment?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
chloe@redwood.com

From: James Liao <james@chalice.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 16:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate & cost/latency/quality rationale for Chalice

Chloe — thanks for the clear breakdown and the bench PDF. Quick clarifying questions:

1) For the summarization route we care most about factuality. How much did GPTJ-13b outperform Mistral-7b on the factuality metric in your runs?
2) The cost numbers look reasonable — are those infra-true costs (including GPU amortization) or Redwood list/charge estimates?

Also, we have an internal security review happening next week. Will the eval cluster generate the standard SOC2 artifact set (logs, access records) we can attach to the review?

On availability — Mon 6/4 10am PT works for me.

—James
Head of Product, Chalice AI
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 19:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate & cost/latency/quality rationale for Chalice

Chloe / Marissa — quick internal notes to prep for Mon:

- Factuality delta: GPTJ-13b shows a ~0.12 higher factuality score on Chalice's summarization subset (we calibrated against the regression set in the attachment). That is material for them, so we should propose a hybrid route where summarize_long defaults to GPTJ but falls back to Mistral for soft-SLOs.
- Cost basis: the numbers Chloe listed are our estimated billed unit costs (includes cloud + infra overhead at current reserved pricing assumptions). I'll attach a short cost sensitivity tab during the pilot.
- Audit logs & SOC2 artifacts: yes, the eval cluster will capture request-level telemetry, role-based access logs, and configured retention. I'll flag Security to prepare the SOC2 evidence package; need Chalice's contact for the NDA if they want deeper access.

Action items:
1) Chloe: finalize the pilot route definitions and sample sizes; include evaluation thresholds for factuality & hallucination.
2) Marissa: prepare the 3-month pilot commercial sheet draft (CH-4721).
3) Karthik: queue a small 4-bit quant trial for GPTJ-13b in staging; target runtime window next week.

Ben
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: James Liao <james@chalice.ai>, Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@chalice.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate & cost/latency/quality rationale for Chalice

Thanks James — quick answers and confirmed next steps below.

1) Factuality: GPTJ-13b + few-shot prompting improved our calibrated factuality metric by +0.12 vs. Mistral on your summarization prompts (see bench_results_chalice_20280601.pdf, page 6). Recommendation: route summarization to GPTJ-13b with a 2-pass check — first-pass generation, second-pass lightweight reranker using the Mistral scoring model to catch high-risk hallucinations.

2) Cost: Ben's right — listed costs reflect Redwood's estimated billed unit cost under current reserved pricing. We'll snapshot assumptions in the cost model (attached) and keep a sensitivity band.

3) Security artifacts: we'll produce standard SOC2 evidence (logs, RBAC exports, request ledger) for the eval cluster. James — please share the security contact + NDA owner and we'll prioritize.

Confirming: Mon 6/4 10:00–10:30am PT for alignment. Agenda: pilot routes + sample sizes (10m tokens), success thresholds (factuality/hallucination), SOC2 contact + NDA, timeline for procurement.

If that looks good I'll ask Sales Ops to issue the 3-month pilot commercial and send a calendar invite.

Best,
Chloe
